Karthik —

Thanks for the packet. Please find Navion's redline attached. High‑level items we flagged:

1) Data retention & locality — we need a clause that requires EU data residency for EU patients (Exhibit F) and a commitment to notify us 60 days before any change in processing location.
2) Termination for convenience — Procurement is pushing for 180 days notice to align with our fiscal planning.
3) SLA credits — we provided suggested thresholds and a simple credit schedule (we prefer a per‑incident credit up to 30% for major outages).
4) Dedicated capacity burst — clarify whether burst capacity is billed as overage or pre‑purchased tokens.

Date: Sun, 04 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Navion renewal: redlines received — internal sync

Team — forwarding Navion's redline. Quick summary and asks:

- Data residency: Navion insists on EU residency language plus a 60‑day notice for changes in processing location.
- Termination for convenience: asking 180 days (we typically accept 90 or 120 for renewals).
- SLA credits: they've proposed per‑incident credits up to 30% — seems high and potentially open to a blended monthly credit cap.
- Capacity billing: they want clarity whether burst is pre‑purchased (they prefer predictable billing).

Could Legal (Soojin) advise on acceptable carve‑outs for regulated customers on residency + notice windows? Lauren/Marcus — can you confirm whether we can offer a burst pre‑purchase option and a way to show a capacity schedule that avoids surprise overages?

Elena — I'm looping internal folks and will come back with proposed compromise language by Tuesday.

Thanks,
Karthik

[Forwarded attachment: Navion_MSA_Redline_20280303.docx]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@navionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Navion renewal: redlines received — internal sync

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the flag. I reviewed Navion_MSA_Redline_20280303.docx and drafted a response with compromise language. Key positions and recommended concessions:

- Data locality: we can accept an Exhibit F addition that requires EU patient data to remain in the EU and a 60‑day notice for material changes in processing location, provided we retain the ability to use reasonable subcontractors and maintain the same security controls (we add an exception for emergency disaster recovery with prior notice).

- Termination for convenience: propose 120 days as middle ground. We should avoid 180 days due to revenue recognition and capacity commitments.

- SLA credits: decline the 30% per incident cap; propose a graduated credit (5% for minor, 15% for major, cumulative monthly cap of 30%) and a maximum annual cap tied to the base subscription value. This preserves predictability.

- Burst capacity: offer a pre‑purchase burst block option (e.g., 10% of committed capacity) billed upfront as an addendum line item. Any overages beyond burst would be billed at an agreed overage rate. Marcus — confirm we can codify a burst SKU and provide the billing schedule for Exhibit D.

I've attached a consolidated response redline with in‑line edits and suggested compromise language. Please review and flag anything non‑starter.

Attached: Redwood_Response_Redline_20280306.docx

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

[Attachment: Redwood_Response_Redline_20280306.docx]

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@navionhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 13:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Navion renewal: follow up on proposed compromises

Soojin / Karthik —

Appreciate the quick review and the proposed language. A couple of items from Procurement that will determine internal approval:

- Termination window: Procurement will only approve 120 days with an explicit exception for budgetary approvals that could require 180 days — can Redwood include a clause that permits a one‑time extension to 180 days if both parties agree in writing within 30 days of execution?
- SLA credits: we like the graduated approach but need clarity on how credits apply to multi‑region incidents where only some customers are affected.
- Burst pre‑purchase: Procurement prefers the burst as a line on the order form (so it's on our PO). Can you produce a draft order form with a 20% burst SKU priced out?

If you can send a consolidated sign‑ready packet with a line item for burst and a DocuSign link, Procurement can route it for signature.

Elena

[Attachment: Navion_Procurement_Form_20280308.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@navionhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@navionhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Navion renewal: consolidated redline and signature packet

Elena —

Thanks for the feedback and for running this with Procurement. Per Soojin's guidance we've accepted 120 days as the standard termination window and included a one‑time extension clause to allow a documented 180‑day extension if both parties sign off within 30 days of execution.

SLA credits: we've added language clarifying multi‑region incidents — credits prorate by impacted region and the cumulative monthly cap still applies.

Burst capacity: Marcus confirmed we can offer a 20% burst SKU priced as a one‑time addendum line item on the order form. Attached is the consolidated redline and a draft order form that includes the burst line.

Next steps:
- DocuSign packet (link below) to be routed to Navion Legal and Procurement.
- Please confirm PO number to populate on the order form.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-navion-renewal
